market_holds: Spot $1.00 at the 2026-11-20 close (intraday low $0.86), 0.4% above the 52-week low and 63% below the high. Market cap about $31m on 32.0m shares (stockanalysis, 2026-11-20). The stock is down about 29% since $1.40 on 2026-11-04 and fell 9% on 2026-11-16, the day the results date was announced. 20-day realised vol is 92%. Volume averages 14k shares a day and was about 1.7k on recent days, so a handful of trades sets the print. There is no option chain, no analyst coverage, no published consensus and no guidance, so no stated bar exists. What the price does reflect is the Q2 trajectory: system SSS -17.8%, revenue -21.7%, adjusted EBITDA margin -7.6%, all published 2026-08-18. The stock fell 18.8% that day and about 20% more over the next two sessions. The last five results days moved -4.2% (Dec 2025), +6.3% (Apr 2026), +0.3% (Jun 2026), -18.8% (Aug 2026) and +3.6% (Aug 2025), from Yahoo daily bars. Funding risk is being met by the parent: Tim Hortons Restaurants International (THRI) bought three US$15m tranches of convertible notes in July, September and October 2026 (6-Ks of 2026-09-10 and 2026-10-19), with a fourth expected in Q1 2027.
view: Q3 2026 is set up to look worse than Q2 on the headline. In Q3 2025 delivery-platform subsidies were at their peak: Tims China's system SSS was +1.3% and company-store SSS +3.3%, against -4.8% and -3.6% in Q2 2025. That makes this quarter's comparison about 6-7 points harder. Q2 2026's two-year stack was about -22.6% system-wide. Luckin's two-year stack worsened by about 5 points from Q2 to Q3 2026 (self-operated SSS went from -5.3% to -11.1% against comps of +13.4% and +14.3%). Applying those two facts, my own arithmetic puts Tims' Q3 system SSS at roughly -24% to -29%, and revenue at about RMB255-280m against RMB358.0m a year earlier, which would be flat to down from Q2's RMB273.4m. Management also said it would step up marketing 'significantly' from September, so the EBITDA loss probably widens before any benefit shows. Against that, the price already holds a lot. It is at all-time lows and has fallen 29% into the print on almost no volume. THRI's funding keeps going-concern risk in the release from being a new shock. A turnaround narrative is possible from the new CEO, who was promising new products 'later in the year': a month-by-month improvement through Q3 into October, as Luckin described for itself, or a new milk-coffee and pricing program. With no consensus to beat, the reaction depends on how a few retail holders read 'SSS -25%' next to whatever the CEO says about October. I lean slightly down, because the visible headline is worse than Q2's and the Q2 reaction shows this holder base sells that. But the drawdown already in the price and the noise in a stock trading 1-2k shares a day keep this well short of a call.
unpriced: Possibly the size of the SSS deterioration. Nobody publishes an estimate, and the comparison is about 6-7 points harder than Q2's because of last year's subsidy peak. That is a mechanical worsening the holder base may not have computed. But the 29% slide into the print may already hold it, and I cannot show either way.

recommendation.reason: The comparison base makes a worse SSS print than Q2 likely (my arithmetic: about -24% to -29% against -17.8%), and the stock fell 18.8% on the Q2 headline. But the stock is already at its low after a 29% slide into the date, the parent's funding removes the solvency shock, and the market is too thin for a 13:00 Monday price to say much. The lean does not reach 65.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A Q3 system SSS better than about -20%, or management saying October SSS improved materially after the September marketing push. Either would read as the turnaround starting and could squeeze this thin float up.

self_critique: The stock already fell 29% into the print and sits at an all-time low, so a bad SSS number may be fully discounted. A new CEO with fresh funding has every reason to lead with improving monthly trends, new products and October data. In a $31m stock trading 1-2k shares a day, a few buy orders could put the Monday 13:00 price well above $1.00. The Q1 2026 print followed the same pattern: down 12.9% on the date notice, then +0.3% on the day. My SSS projection is also arithmetic, and Tims' heavier September marketing may have closed some of the gap.
approach_notes: The P6 advice to find the line and rebuild it from counterparties paid off: Luckin's disclosure plus the year-ago base gave a concrete SSS estimate. P4's 'priced is a claim to prove' cuts both ways here: with no consensus I could not show the bad SSS was priced, nor that it was not. In a stock this illiquid the window price is mostly noise, and the playbook has no guidance for that case.
